Offline chat exchanges text and short audio messages between phones on the same Wi-Fi network or on one phone's hotspot, even without internet.

• Whoever creates the channel is its owner and decides who joins: each phone must be approved by the owner. The owner can remove anyone at any time. Only approve people you know.
• Messages are end-to-end encrypted between each phone and the owner's phone, which relays them to the others. They don't go through any server of the developers or third parties, or through the internet.
• Messages are not stored: they disappear when the chat screen is closed. Only the channel name and the list of approved phones are kept.
• The channel name is visible to anyone on the same network: don't use personal data in it.
• The microphone is only used while you hold the talk button.
• The range is short (usually inside the house or building) and depends on the network, the battery and the owner's phone having the channel open. Don't use it as your main means in an emergency: call 193 or 192 (Brazil).
• You are responsible for what you send. Don't use the chat to offend, threaten or deceive anyone.

• The data is kept in a database in the app's private area on your device, protected by the system and encrypted. • Sharing with another phone and Offline chat are optional and happen directly between the devices, on the same Wi-Fi network, encrypted (see items 16 and 18).

The breathing, stretching, eye-break and relaxation exercises are general everyday wellbeing guidance. They are not treatment, physiotherapy or rehabilitation and do not replace an assessment by a doctor or physiotherapist.

Where they come from: the exercises are based on public guidance from well-known health institutions and simply adapted for the app: neck and shoulder stretches from Mayo Clinic (USA) and the NHS (the UK public health service); eye breaks from the American Academy of Ophthalmology's 20-20-20 rule; slow breathing from the NHS; "Box" breathing (4-4-4-4) as described by Cleveland Clinic; "Calm" breathing (4-7-8) by Dr. Andrew Weil; and guided body-part relaxation, as in NHS materials. These institutions have no connection with Rotina Aí and have not reviewed or endorsed the app.

• Move slowly, without forcing and only as far as is comfortable. Stretching shouldn't hurt.
• If you feel pain, tingling, numbness, dizziness, shortness of breath or any discomfort, stop right away and breathe normally. If the pain continues, comes back or gets worse, see a doctor or physiotherapist.
• Talk to a doctor or physiotherapist before doing the exercises if you have back or neck problems (such as a herniated disc), a recent injury or surgery, osteoporosis, labyrinthitis or frequent dizziness, uncontrolled high blood pressure, heart or lung problems, or if you are pregnant.
• In the breathing rhythms where you hold your breath ("Box" and "Calm"), people with heart or lung problems, high blood pressure or who are pregnant should prefer "Gentle" or "Balance" and not hold their breath.
• Do the exercises sitting down or somewhere safe. Don't do them while driving or in situations that need your attention.
• The animated figure shows the movement in a simplified way: respect your body's limits.

entries.q: What does Rotina Aí do?
entries.a: Rotina Aí helps you, alone or with your family, take care of everyday life: reminders for water, exercise, meals, breaks, sleep and anything else you want; a family calendar linked to Google Calendar; birthdays with gift ideas; a memory book with audio and photos; family documents (vaccination card, receipts and warranties, school); shopping list and monthly budget; a scam protection pact; weight and cycle; relaxation exercises with calm music; the day's weather and the SOS button. Everything stays on your phone.

entries.q: Does the app work without internet?
entries.a: Yes! Almost everything works without internet: reminders, shopping, budget, birthdays, memories, documents, cycle, weight and Capi. The internet is only used for the weather, ads, cloud backup and, if you use it, for your Google or iCloud calendar to sync with the family.

entries.q: Is my data safe? Who sees my data?
also: who has access to my data
entries.a: Your data stays only on your phone, protected by the app password: reminders, measurements, budget, memories, documents, everything. The developers have no server that receives this data: we don't see it, sell it or share it. The details are in the Privacy policy, in Settings.

entries.q: Does the app give a diagnosis or replace the doctor?
entries.a: No. Rotina Aí is informational: it organizes your routine and explains data, but it doesn't diagnose or prescribe. Any decision about health or medicines should be discussed with a doctor or pharmacist.

entries.q: Does the app have medicine reminders, vaccines or a medical card?
entries.a: This version of Rotina Aí takes care of routine and wellbeing: water, exercise, meals, breaks, sleep, weight, cycle, calendar, birthdays and memories. Vaccine schedule, medical card and hospital list aren't part of this version. You can keep a copy of the vaccination card (photo or PDF) in Home → Documents. In an emergency, use the SOS button or call your local emergency number.

entries.q: How do I contact the app's developer?
entries.a: You can write to loboguaratec@gmail.com. The terms of use and privacy policy are in Settings.

entries.q: Is the app free?
entries.a: Yes, the app is free and is kept running by discreet ads. Anyone who wants can become an "App Supporter": no ads and the 💚 badge. Tap "support us and remove ads", just below the ad banner. No feature is locked.

entries.q: How do I mark a reminder as done?
entries.a: On the Today screen, the "Now" card shows the next reminder: tap "I drank", "I did it", "I ate" or "Done". If you won't do it that day, tap "Skip today".

entries.q: How do I change or delete a reminder?
entries.a: In the Reminders tab, tap the reminder to change the name, detail, icon, times and days. To delete it, tap the trash can at the top of the reminder screen.

entries.q: How do I choose a reminder's icon?
entries.a: On the reminder screen, tap the icon square next to the title. The icons are grouped: personal care, food and water, movement, sleep, home, family and pets, school and work, dates.

entries.q: How do I pause a reminder without deleting it?
entries.a: In the Reminders tab, use the switch next to the reminder: when it's off, it stops notifying you but stays saved for when you want to turn it back on.

entries.q: How do I set a reminder to drink water?
entries.a: In the Reminders tab, tap "New reminder" and choose "Water". You choose when to start, when to stop and how often you want to be reminded. On the Today screen, each person's water glasses fill up with each tap.

entries.q: How do I change the alarm sound?
entries.a: Open the reminder in the Reminders tab and tap "Alert sound" to choose another sound. The app's sounds (water, celebrations) are in Settings → Sounds and vibration.

entries.q: The reminder isn't ringing. What do I do?
entries.a: Check three things: 1) whether the reminder is on (switch in the Reminders tab); 2) whether the app has notification permission in the phone settings; 3) whether the phone's battery saver isn't blocking Rotina Aí. On some phones you need to set the app's battery use to "unrestricted".

entries.q: How do I do the guided breathing?
entries.a: On the Today screen, in the "Relax" block, tap "Breathe" (it is also in Family → person → "Relax"). Pick a rhythm (Gentle, Box, Calm or Balance) and tap "Start". The circle grows when it's time to breathe in, holds when it's time to hold and shrinks when it's time to breathe out. It takes about 1 minute. You can pick some calm music too. If you feel dizzy, stop and breathe normally.

entries.q: What exercises are in Relax? Can I have music?
entries.a: The Today screen has a "Relax" block with shortcuts to Breathe, Stretch, Eyes and 1-minute break. Under "See all exercises and music" you'll also find Guided relaxation (3 min) and the music choice: Calm sea, Light rain, Soft chords or all in a loop. The 🔊 speaker mutes the music. They are general wellbeing guidance based on institutions such as Mayo Clinic, the NHS (UK) and the American Academy of Ophthalmology (see "Where these exercises come from"). If you feel pain, stop; if the pain continues, see a doctor or physiotherapist. To do it with your eyes closed, turn on "🔔 Soft bell" and/or "📳 Vibrate": they signal each step change.

entries.q: How do I use birthdays?
entries.a: In the Family tab, tap "Birthdays" and "New birthday" (or "Bring in the family's birthdays"). Write down the date, likes, sizes and gift ideas. The app reminds you before (you choose how long) and on the day, with ready-made messages to send on WhatsApp. In "Gifts already given" you note what you gave, so you don't repeat it.

entries.q: How does the Memory book work?
entries.a: In the Family tab, tap "Memory book". Choose the person (for example, grandma), tap "Answer" and record the answer in her voice, take a photo or write. You can skip the question or tell something freely. With the book button at the top, the app builds a PDF with the stories and sends the audio along. Everything stays only on the phone and is included in the backup.

entries.q: Where do I keep the vaccination card, receipts and warranties?
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "Family documents" and choose the person. The vaccination card is at the top: photograph the front and back or save the digital certificate PDF. In "Add document" you keep receipts and warranties (with the date, the app shows when it's out of warranty), manuals, electricity bills, school papers, certificates, membership cards and the pet's vaccines. Everything stays only on the phone, encrypted with the app password, and is included in the encrypted backup. Don't store ID cards, tax numbers, driver's licenses or bank cards.

entries.q: How does the app help against scams?
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "Scam protection pact". Add up to 3 trusted people, check the family's agreements and do the 1-minute practice each week. If you get a strange request for money, a code or a link, tap "I'm not sure": the app shows what to do and calls someone you trust. The family's secret word isn't stored in the app, on purpose: agree on it out loud.

entries.q: How do I add trusted people?
also: who to send my location to
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "Scam protection pact" and "Add trusted person" (up to 3, with name and phone). They appear in "I'm not sure" so you can call them, and they receive your location when you use SOS.

entries.q: How does the family calendar work?
entries.a: In the Family tab, tap "Family calendar" and "Choose the calendar". The app uses your phone's calendars: choose a "Family" calendar shared on Google Calendar (or iCloud, on iPhone) and everyone sees the events on their own phone. Then just tap "New event": outing, school and enrollment, party, trip… The calendar screen has step-by-step instructions to create and share the calendar on Google.

entries.q: How do I use the shopping list?
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "Shopping list" and "New list" (you can add a date). Type the items: the app sorts them by supermarket section and suggests what you usually buy. At the store, check off what you picked up and, if you want, note the price. You can send the list on WhatsApp, repeat the list and, when you finish, record the total in the monthly budget.

entries.q: How does the monthly budget work?
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "Monthly budget" and "Add": choose income or expense, the amount and the category. Check "Fixed every month" for salary, rent and bills and use "Add this month's fixed entries". With your history, the app shows the average of the last months and an estimate of how much you'll spend until the end of the month. It's only for notes: it doesn't connect to banks and everything stays on the phone.

entries.q: How do I add a family member?
entries.a: Go to the Family tab and tap "Add family member", or "+ Add" next to the photos at the top of the screens. Each person has their own reminders, measurements and cycle.

entries.q: How do I see another family member's things?
entries.a: Tap the person's face in the row of photos at the top of the Today and Reminders screens. Everything shown switches to them. In the Family tab, tapping the person opens their page, with reminders and wellbeing.

entries.q: How do I change someone's details or delete a person?
entries.a: In the Family tab, tap the pencil next to the person to edit name, date of birth, height and other details. You can also delete their profile there.

entries.q: How do I record my weight?
entries.a: The quickest way: on the Today screen, in the "Wellbeing" block, tap "Weight". You can also go to the Family tab: tap the person and, under "Measurements", tap the weight card (or "Add") and enter the value. Tapping the card shows the chart and history. To see your BMI, add the height in the person's profile.

entries.q: Does the app tell me whether my measurement is good or bad?
entries.a: No. The app keeps your measurements, shows the chart and the general reference for adults (with the source, such as the World Health Organization for BMI), but doesn't evaluate your values. Take the history to your doctor.

entries.q: How do I see the chart of my measurements?
entries.a: On the Today screen, in the "Wellbeing" block, tap "Weight" and then the weight card to open the chart and history. You can also go to the Family tab: tap the person and "Measurements".

entries.q: How do I track my period and cycle?
entries.a: On the Today screen, in the "Wellbeing" block, tap "Cycle" (or, in the Family tab, tap the person and "Cycle"). Mark "Period started" on the first day and, if you like, the flow and symptoms. The app learns from your cycles and shows predictions. If you use a hormonal method, mark it in the cycle settings.

entries.q: Does the app show the fertile window or ovulation?
entries.a: No. This version of Rotina Aí doesn't calculate the fertile window or ovulation: it only shows the prediction of your next period, based on the average of your cycles. To avoid or plan a pregnancy, talk to a gynecologist or your health service.

entries.q: Does the app read my DNA?
entries.a: No. This version of Rotina Aí doesn't read DNA files or do genetic analysis. To understand a genetic test, talk to a doctor or a geneticist.

entries.q: How does the SOS button work?
entries.a: The red SOS button is at the top of the Today screen. There you call your country's emergency numbers by sliding the button (it prevents calls by mistake), send your location by WhatsApp or SMS to your trusted people and open the hospital search on the map.

entries.q: How do I send my location to someone?
entries.a: In SOS, tap "Send my location" (WhatsApp or SMS). The message includes your name and a map link and goes to the trusted people you added in the "Scam protection pact" (or you choose the contact at the time). SMS works even without internet.

entries.q: How do I back up my data?
entries.a: In Settings there are two options: "Cloud backup" (one backup a day, encrypted, in your Google Drive) and "File backup" (you keep the file wherever you want). Both use the app password. When you change phones, install the app and restore the backup.

entries.q: How do I recover my data from a backup?
entries.a: In Settings, use "Restore backup" (file) or go to "Cloud backup" → "Restore backup now". Note: this replaces the data on this phone with the backup's, and asks for the app password.

entries.q: I forgot the app password. Now what?
entries.a: The password protects your data with encryption and can't be recovered: not even we can open it without it. If you use phone unlock (fingerprint or face), try that. If there's no way, the only option is to erase and start over: the data and old backups become inaccessible.

entries.q: How do I change the app password?
entries.a: In Settings → "Password and security", tap "Change password". Future backups will use the new password.

entries.q: How do I open the app with fingerprint or face?
entries.a: In Settings → "Password and security: how to open the app", choose "Phone unlock". If the fingerprint or face fails, the app asks for the password you created.

entries.q: How do I delete all my data?
entries.a: In Settings, at the bottom of the screen, tap "Delete all my data". There's no going back: make a backup first if you want to keep anything. Uninstalling the app also deletes the data on this phone.

entries.q: How do I make the text bigger?
entries.a: In Settings → Appearance, use "Text and icon size" (Small, Normal, Large or Extra large). It applies to the whole app and adds to the phone's font size.

entries.q: How do I make the app dark?
entries.a: In Settings → Appearance, choose "Dark", "Light" or "System" (follows the phone).

entries.q: How do I hide a block on the Today screen?
entries.a: Tap the little arrows in the corner of each block's title: it becomes a single line. Tap again to open it. The app remembers your choice.

entries.q: How do I change the weather city or use my neighborhood?
entries.a: Tap the city name on the weather card (or Settings → "City and weather"). Choose the city or tap "Use my location" to see your neighborhood's weather; the position is rounded and isn't stored. The Today screen card shows the temperature and the day's tips.

entries.q: How do I remove the ads?
entries.a: Become an "App Supporter": tap "support us and remove ads", below the ad banner, or go to Settings → "App Supporter". The subscription is yearly or monthly through your phone's store. You can also support the app by watching a short video now and then.

entries.q: How do I cancel the Supporter subscription?
entries.a: In Settings → "App Supporter", tap "Manage or cancel subscription": it opens the store page (Google Play) where you cancel. Changed phones? Use "Restore purchase" on the same screen.

entries.q: How do I change the app language?
entries.a: Go to Settings → 🌎 Language and pick a language. The app uses it the next time it opens. If you leave it on "Phone's language", it follows the phone. Dates and money follow the phone's region.

entries.q: How do I turn off the app sounds and vibration?
entries.a: Go to Settings → 🔊 Sounds and vibration and turn off "Sounds" (water, reminder done and celebrations) or "Vibration". App sounds respect the phone's silent mode. The reminder sound is changed in each reminder, in the Reminders tab. The Relax music has its own 🔊 button.

entries.q: How do I share the shopping list or expenses with another phone?
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "🔗 Share with another phone". First pair the two phones (only once): one taps "This phone waits" and shows a QR code; the other taps "Look for the other phone", then "Scan QR code" and points the camera. Without a camera, you can type the 8-digit code shown under the QR and check the security code. Then open the list and tap ⋮ → "Share with…". To sync, both phones must be on the same Wi-Fi and both people tap "Allow". Nothing goes through the internet or a server: it travels encrypted straight from one phone to the other.

entries.q: Who can change a shared list? What needs approval?
entries.a: Whoever created the list (or entered the expense) owns it and can change it freely. If the other person adds, removes or changes items on your list, or touches your expenses, it only goes in if you approve when syncing. Checking ✔ bought and noting the price go in directly. If the same thing changed on both phones, the owner chooses. From the list menu you can send your version, get the other one, send a copy, stop sharing or delete on both. You can also undo the last sync on the sharing screen.

entries.q: How do I put together the family emergency kit?
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "🎒 Prepared family". Tap "Build the kit from the suggested list", choose the items and check what you already have. Add the expiry date to items that expire: the app reminds you 30 days before. The calculator shows how much water and food to store for your household (at least 3 days), and "Add what's missing to the shopping list" creates the list for the store. You'll also find the family plan (meeting points and who to tell) and short guides on water, food, power outages, floods and heat, based on public civil defense and health guidance. In an emergency, follow the authorities and call emergency services.

entries.q: How do I talk to my family without internet?
entries.a: In the Home tab, tap "🎒 Prepared family" and then "📻 Offline chat". One person taps "Create channel" and keeps the screen open. The others, on the same Wi-Fi network (or on one phone's hotspot, which works without internet), tap the channel under "Channels on this network" and ask to join. The channel creator approves each phone; next time it joins directly. To talk, hold the microphone button and release to send. Messages are encrypted, don't go through the internet and aren't stored. The range is short: in an emergency, call emergency services.

entries.q: Does the app have an SOS flashlight or whistle?
entries.a: Yes. In Home → "🎒 Prepared family" → "SOS light and whistle": the screen can turn white (like a flashlight) or slowly flash the SOS signal, and the phone can whistle 3 times in a row, the distress signal. Turn up the brightness and volume. The phone's own flashlight, in quick settings, is brighter and uses less battery.
